local.h: Ballot measure would create fund for 911 upgrades
local.b: A proposed constitutional amendment would create a dedicated fund lawmakers could use to modernize Georgia's 911 system, though it would not allocate any money itself.
local.title: Ballot amendment would pave the way for dedicated funding to upgrade Georgia’s 911 system

local.h: Georgia tackles rural maternal health crisis
local.b: With labor and delivery units closing in rural Georgia, some expectant mothers face long drives to give birth.
local.title: Georgia gears up to solve rural maternal health crisis

local.h: Georgia daycares keep high ratings despite violations
local.b: An AJC investigation found daycares where children were hurt or put at risk kept or improved their state quality ratings, and some still get taxpayer funding.
local.title: Georgia daycares receive high ratings despite injuries and safety violations

local.h: Atlanta council advances jail sale despite pushback
local.b: The City Council sent legislation to sell the roughly 1,300-bed Atlanta City Detention Center to Fulton County to the mayor, despite opposition.
local.title: 'Hot potato-ing a building': Atlanta City Council advances jail sale despite pushback

local.b: A Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll of 500 registered voters found three of the nine ballot questions, including all-party primaries, in a virtual tie two weeks before Election Day.

local.h: Johnson budget would reopen mental health clinic
local.b: Mayor Brandon Johnson's 2027 budget would reopen a city mental health clinic and spend $5 million to make the CARE crisis response program permanent.
local.title: Mayor Johnson budget seeks to reopen city mental health clinic next year

local.h: Fearing ICE, some immigrants shift life to night
local.b: Some Chicago immigrants now wait until nighttime to do laundry, shop and work to avoid immigration enforcement.
local.title: Fearing ICE, some Chicago immigrants shift work, daily life to nighttime hours

local.h: What a stressed grid means for Illinois customers
local.b: WBEZ's Curious City looks at the strain on Illinois' electric grid and what it could mean for consumers.
local.title: Illinois’ electric grid is under a lot of stress. What does that mean for consumers?

local.h: Shedd CEO: five beluga deaths not a crisis
local.b: Five belugas have died at Shedd Aquarium since Aug. 25. CEO Bridget Coughlin defended rescuing 10 whales from Marineland in Canada.
local.title: Five beluga whales have died at Shedd since Aug. 25, but CEO Bridget Coughlin says this is no crisis

local.h: SEIU backs Giannoulias in Chicago mayor's race
local.b: SEIU Locals 1 and 73, which gave over $4.5 million to Mayor Johnson's 2023 campaign, endorsed Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias.

local.h: Chicago mayoral hopefuls file petition stacks
local.b: Candidates wheeled in thousands of nominating petitions at the start of a weeklong filing period for the February election. They need 12,500 valid signatures.

local.h: Endangered Species Act changes threaten Illinois species
local.b: Trump administration changes to how the law is interpreted could put 24 endangered and 12 threatened species in Illinois at greater risk.

local.h: Experts: don't panic over DOJ voter fraud suit
local.b: Election experts told LAist the federal lawsuit seeking to remove alleged noncitizens from California's rolls is unlikely to succeed and voters should fill out ballots as normal.
local.title: Feds are suing California over voter fraud allegations. Experts tell voters: Don’t freak out

local.h: Bass seeks pause on DWP shutoffs through 2026
local.b: After record heat waves, Mayor Bass asked LADWP to pause residential shutoffs for nonpayment through year's end. The utility says it takes effect immediately.
local.title: Can't pay your LADWP bill? LA mayor announces a pause on utility shutoffs

local.h: $125M settlement approved for Garden Grove tank
local.b: GKN Aerospace will fund up to $100 million in claims for residents and businesses forced out when about 50,000 people evacuated over the failing chemical tank.
local.title: $125M settlement approved for Garden Grove chemical tank incident

local.h: LA County emergency official sues over Eaton Fire
local.b: Nicholas Vaquero of the Office of Emergency Management alleges retaliation after he complained the county failed to properly staff its response to the deadly Eaton Fire.
local.title: Emergency manager sues LA County, alleging retaliation over Eaton Fire whistleblower complaints

local.h: Brad Lander freed after West Bank detention
local.b: Brad Lander, Democratic nominee for NY-10, said Israeli forces detained him while he helped Palestinian farmers pick olives, then released him Wednesday morning.
local.title: Brad Lander says he's released after Israeli forces detained him during olive harvest

local.h: 3,000 families get childcare vouchers off waitlist
local.b: The Mamdani administration is notifying 3,000 families that they can get subsidized childcare vouchers. Nearly 30,000 are on the waitlist.
local.title: NYC’s subsidized childcare waitlist is moving, starting with 3K families

local.h: Musk spends $500K to re-elect Rep. Mike Lawler
local.b: Elon Musk has spent more than $500,000 backing Lawler in his competitive Hudson Valley race against Democrat Cait Conley.
local.title: Elon Musk drops $500K on NY Rep. Mike Lawler's re-election bid

local.h: Schools chancellor offers no integration plan
local.b: Chancellor Kamar Samuels said the Mamdani administration is committed to integrating NYC public schools but declined to share a specific plan, drawing groans from a frustrated crowd.
local.title: Parents grumble as NYC schools chancellor dodges calls for NYC schools integration plan

local.h: GWB shooting victim dies; no arrests yet
local.b: A 46-year-old man shot while driving on the George Washington Bridge has died. Police say it appears to stem from road rage and no arrests have been made. All lanes reopened Wednesday.
local.title: George Washington Bridge reopens after fatal shooting; no arrests made

local.h: NYC proposes rules for AI customer service bots
local.b: A proposed rule would require businesses to disclose AI chatbots and let customers talk to a person instead. The city says it is the first of its kind.
local.title: NYC proposes crackdown down on AI customer service chatbots

goodnews.h: Coney Island's 1890s lighthouse may be landmarked
goodnews.b: The Landmarks Preservation Commission voted to hold a hearing on the 70-foot lighthouse, which has guided boats for more than 135 years, and its keeper's house.
goodnews.title: Coney Island's small, 1890s lighthouse may be landmarked by the city

local.h: French government websites down after hacking alert
local.b: Tax and préfecture websites went down and Météo France took its sites offline after a critical vulnerability was found in the PHP programming language.
local.title: French government websites down after hacking alert

local.h: Orange hit by nationwide phone and internet outage
local.b: Orange said a nationwide incident was severely disrupting calls, texts and mobile internet, with thousands of reports logged by midday.
local.title: France's Orange network hit by phone and internet outage

local.h: Arrest, anti-terror probe over Limoges town hall fire
local.b: Police arrested a man believed linked to the ultra-left and called in anti-terror investigators over the fire that collapsed the 1883 town hall's roof and belfry during weekend rioting.

local.h: Council restricts overnight RV parking
local.b: The Seattle City Council passed a package limiting RVs to two hours of street parking starting next year and aiming to steer vehicle residents into shelter and services.

local.h: Ferguson: repeal of millionaires tax would hike daycare costs
local.b: Gov. Ferguson says repealing the 9.9% tax on household income over $1 million would cut child care subsidies used by about 51,000 children.

local.h: 250,000 in Washington could lose Medicaid
local.b: New Medicaid work requirements for low-income adults start in January, and up to 250,000 Washington residents could lose coverage.
